plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/22844
Crypto-theft coding convention used throughout this batch: stolen funds coded as confidentiality data variety Virtual currency (data_victim Victim organization unless customer wallets were drained), integrity Fraudulent transaction for the unauthorized transfers, and the USD loss in impact (Asset and fraud). Template Hacking-ext-unknown used; asset S - Other (exchange Solana wallets) and vector Unknown. The sources read give no method and no attribution (The Register only notes Upbit was previously targeted by North Korea); actor external Unknown, Financial. Data_victim includes Customer since the exchange held customer assets (Upbit pledged to cover losses per wider reporting; not in the sources read).
Impact 44.5B won ~ $30.2M. Discovery internal Unknown (emergency meeting 18 minutes after detecting the activity). Victim: Dunamu Inc. (Upbit), KR, NAICS 523150 (issue 522), headcount 101 to 1000 (roughly 600 staff; estimate). dbir_year 2027.

summary: Between 4:42 and 5:36 a.m. on November 27, 2025 about 104 billion Solana-based tokens (mostly BONK) worth about 44.5 billion won ($30 million) were withdrawn from Korean crypto exchange Upbit, operated by Dunamu, to unknown external wallets. Upbit suspended Solana deposits and withdrawals and later halted all digital asset transactions; it reported to the FSS about six hours after the breach. The theft came one day after Naver announced it would acquire Dunamu.
